question.text: During the 1970s in this country, bordering Thailand and Vietnam, the Khmer Rouge under Pol Pot headed a genocide now referred to as the Killing Fields.
question.clue: Millions of people were killed in the 1970s under Pol Pot, who led this country's Khmer Rouge regime.

swap.leadin: Mark Twain wrote a satirical "Defense of" a man who dressed as a scout to capture a leader of this country, Frederick Funston.
swap.text: Name this country whose Moro people resisted US occupation while led by Emilio Aguinaldo. After an 1898 conflict, colonial rule over this Asian country was ceded by a European power.
swap.clue: An American occupation of this nation was resisted by the islamic Moro people and revolutionaries led by Emilio Aguinaldo.

question.leadin: This woman won the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize but could not accept it in person, as the ruling military junta held her under house arrest.
question.text: Name this activist and politician who became State Counsellor of her country in 2016. Since her rise to power, she has been heavily criticized for her inaction against the persecution of the Rohingya people.
question.answerHtml: Aung San Suu Kyi ([ong sahn soo chee], but be lenient) (prompt on “Suu” or “Kyi” alone)
question.clue: This leader allegedly called two Reuters journalists "traitors" after they were arrested while investigating the Inn Din Massacre.

swap.leadin: This site, built by Khmer emperor Suryavarman II, was designed to resemble Mount Meru, the home of the gods in Hinduism.
swap.text: Name this temple complex near the city of Siem Reap, the largest religious structure in the world.
swap.clue: It was originally believed to have been conceived by the god Indra for his son, but most historians agree that construction was initiated by Suryavarman II.

question.leadin: Malcolm Browne won a Pulitzer Prize for his photograph of an event in this city.
question.text: Name this city in which Thich Quang Duc killed himself during South Vietnam's Buddhist Crisis. This city, South Vietnam's capital, was renamed after its fall to the North in 1975.
question.clue: It's not in the United States, but a speech given in this city in 1945 begins, "All men are created equal. They are endowed by their creator with certain inalienable rights..."

swap.leadin: A king in this modern-day country apocryphally killed the prince Mingyi Swa in a 1593 duel.
swap.text: Name this country where King Naresuan ruled the Kingdom of Ayutthaya. The Chakri dynasty would later take power in this country under the leadership of Rama I.
swap.clue: Its rulers used the Paknam Incident to create an irredentist nationalism later deployed by the Phibun government.

question.leadin: This man was captured by General Frederic Funston in the aftermath of the Battle of Tirad Pass.
question.text: Name this revolutionary leader who was brought back to his country by Admiral George Dewey after the Battle of Manila Bay. This man was the first president of a country that would later gain independence due to the Tydings-McDuffie Act.
question.clue: His followers killed potential rival General Antonio Luna to insure that he would lead them into such battles as the one at Tirad Pass.

swap.text: This war-torn country got money raised in concerts organized by Waldheim and Paul McCartney. It has been ruled by Pol Pot and his Khmer Rouge.
swap.answerHtml: Kingdom of Cambodia [or Democratic Kampuchea; or Preăh Réachéanachâk Kâmpŭchéa]
swap.clue: Another temple in this country has large towers adorned with faces called Bayon.

question.text: This ruler was unable to conquer Dai-Viet, but did sack the Champa capital Vijaya. He is best known, however, for the creation of Beng Mealea and another complex dedicated to Vishnu. For 15 points, identify this ruler of the Khmer Empire, who oversaw the construction of Ankgor Wat.
question.clue: The Khmer built the world's largest religious complex at Angkor Wat under this ruler, who is depicted in massive stone heads around the building. This ruler befriended the Chola Dynasty.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Indonesian trading empires.
swap.text: This largest Buddhist temple in the world was constructed under the Javanese Sailendra Dynasty. This temple is divided into sections which represent the three spheres central to Buddhism.
swap.clue: Depictions of Javanese vessels that were used for trade along the Maritime Silk Road can be found in reliefs at this Indonesian temple complex, generally considered the largest Buddhist temple in the world.

question.text: This city was the de facto capital of the Dutch East Indies, when it was known as Batavia. After the Second World War, Sukarno made this city his country's capital.
question.clue: Government buildings are housed near its enormous Merdeka Square, which is home to the flame-topped Monas obelisk.

swap.leadin: This invasion targeted 36 of the 44 provincial capitals of one polity, and led to a massacre at the ancient capital of Hue.
swap.text: Name this North Vietnamese offensive which took place on the namesake holiday, also known as the Vietnamese New Year
swap.clue: A picture taken by Eddie Adams during this military campaign depicts a man in a plaid shirt with a snub-nosed pistol to his head.

question.leadin: Answer the following related to the Taungoo ("TOWN-goo") Empire, an early modern state in Southeast Asia.
question.text: The Taungoo Empire and its successor states, including the Konbaung dynasty, were both based out of this modern-day country later governed from Mandalay by the British.
question.clue: It was ruled by a council called the Hluttaw during its three namesake wars with Britain, and its anti-colonialist movements included the Saya San rebellion and the Thakin party.

swap.text: General Harold Briggs approved the use of this chemical to destroy jungles during the Malayan Emergency. It was more famously used in the Vietnam War.
swap.clue: This carcinogen and defoliant that the United States used in an attempt to increase the visibility of Viet Cong troops.

question.leadin: A king of this dynasty founded an order of Buddhism called Dhammayut and served as the first abbot of the Wat Bowonniwet Vihara.
question.text: Name this dynasty whose viceroy Pinklao was the younger brother of King Mongkut, who negotiated the Bowring Treaty liberalizing foreign trade.
question.clue: This dynasty's first ruler solidified power by winning the Nine Armies War, and it allowed free trade within its territory by agreeing to the Bowring Treaty, which replaced the Burney Treaty.

swap.leadin: This treaty allowed the free importation of opium by British ships into a certain country, mirroring the 'unequal treaties' earlier imposed upon Qing ['ching'] China.
swap.text: Name this 1855 treaty negotiated between its namesake, then the Governor of Hong Kong, and a certain Southeast Asian kingdom, which among other things allowed free trade by foreigners in Bangkok.

question.leadin: A ruler from this family often held court with his pet orangutan Betsy, and he once held a trial in which he sentenced a man-eating crocodile to "be instantly killed without honours."
question.text: Name this royal family, whose rule began when Omar Ali Saifuddin II granted its patriarch territory around the modern-day city of Kuching and the region of Bau. As rulers, they were known as the "White Rajahs."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the rise and fall of the Nguyen Dynasty in Vietnam.
swap.text: With the help of some French troops raised by Pigneau de Behaine, his man united Vietnam and became the first emperor of the Nguyen Dynasty in 1802, proclaiming its capital at Hue and setting up a Confucian state.

question.text: Mandatory collective farming was abandoned in 1988 as part of the Đoi Moi reforms, which were implemented after the death of this successor to Ho Chi Minh as General Secretary.
question.clue: This successor of Ho Chi Minh as Vietnam's general secretary, who oversaw the Cambodian-Vietnamese and Sino-Vietnamese wars. He shared his surname with a dynasty that nominally ruled Đai Viet from 1427 to 1789 despite Mac opposition.

swap.text: One of the few Westerners killed by slow slicing was Joseph Marchand, who was killed in this city in 1835 after joining the Le Van Khoi revolt. Later, the Viet Cong and People's Army of Vietnam massacred thousands of people in this city for 26 days during the Tet Offensive.
swap.clue: This city where the Phat Dan shootings instigated the Buddhist crisis. This city was the site of the longest and bloodiest battle during the Tet Offensive that occurred five years later.
